rationale: Recurring fourth cosmological property (after body / taste / fruit) of each world-king in the five-world Manichaean schema. Each king has a ⲡⲓⲧⲛⲁ which is the metal element 'reigning today' in earthly principalities, doctrines, idolatry, baptisms — i.e. the king's worldly extension/manifestation. Etymology uncertain: possibly from ⲉⲓⲧⲛ̄ 'lower part' (the king's lower-self extending into the world below), or from ϯ 'give' (the king's giving/manifestation). Translation tentative.

Metal/mineral paired with lead (ⲧⲁⲍⲧ) as the substance of the king of Darkness's body. Possibly Greek βάσανος 'touchstone' (a dark stone used to assay gold), or an unidentified Lycopolitan metallurgical term. The double-metal pattern parallels the smoke-world (gold + lead). Tentative.
Greek θηρίον 'wild beast,' plural. The lambda-for-rho substitution is a known Lycopolitan/Manichaean orthographic feature. The lion is described as the foremost (ⲍⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲧ) of all wild beasts.

Compound: ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who') + ⲭⲁⲩ-ⲙⲁⲓ̈ⲧ ('shows the way' from ϫⲱ + ⲙⲟⲉⲓⲧ 'path'). Listed alongside ⲙⲉⲓⲍⲱⲛ (magnates) as a class of worldly authorities under the principalities and powers. Functional equivalent of 'guides, leaders.'
Lycopolitan reflex of ϣⲟⲣⲡ̄ 'first.' Used substantively here for the lion as 'foremost of all wild beasts.'

Coptic noun related to ⲕⲱⲍ/ⲕⲁⲑⲏⲧ 'be set, established' — 'that on which one rests' = trust/confidence. Paired here with ⲍⲉⲗⲡⲓⲥ (ἐλπίς 'hope') as a hendiadys for the baptizers' spiritual reliance on water-baptism.
